rationale: The literature characterizes Stolerman neurodevelopmental syndrome (caused by pathogenic KDM6B variants) primarily by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, ADHD/autistic traits, and non-specific craniofacial dysmorphisms. Features such as severe congenital limb reduction defects, prominent lower eyelid eversion (hallmark of Kabuki syndrome associated with KDM6A/KMT2D), fifth digit aplasia, corneal clouding, and profound prenatal dwarfism are consistently absent across reported clinical cohorts and case series.

evidence.text: Stolerman et al. evaluated 12 unrelated individuals with de novo KDM6B alterations who exhibited intellectual disability, developmental delay, and mild/variable dysmorphic facial features without evidence of severe congenital limb reductions, corneal clouding, or primordial dwarfism.

source.title: Genetic variants in the KDM6B gene are associated with neurodevelopmental delays and dysmorphic features
source.quote: We have identified a number of de novo alterations in the KDM6B gene via whole exome sequencing (WES) in a cohort of 12 unrelated patients with developmental delay, intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, and other clinical findings.

evidence.text: A clinical case report of an individual harboring a de novo KDM6B frameshift variant identified neurodevelopmental disorder with ADHD and subtle dysmorphic facial features, confirming absence of severe ectodermal, limb reduction, or ocular clouding abnormalities.

source.title: The KDM6B mutation: Phenotype and clinical characteristics—Report of a case
source.quote: A frameshift variant in the KDM6B gene related to neurodevelopmental disorders with facial and body dysmorphia was obtained. The case was oriented as a neurodevelopmental disorder secondary to a genetic alteration and a comorbid Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD).

new_directions.question_text: What specific facial dysmorphic metrics reliably distinguish Stolerman syndrome (KDM6B) from Kabuki syndrome types 1 and 2 (KMT2D and KDM6A)?
new_directions.rationale: KDM6A and KDM6B share related demethylase functions, but Kabuki syndrome features lower eyelid eversion and fingertip pads which are putative exclusion criteria for Stolerman syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: Does the frequency of ophthalmologic and digital anomalies differ significantly between truncating/loss-of-function and missense variants in KDM6B?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing genotype-phenotype correlations will confirm whether hypomorphic or dominant-negative missense variants can produce atypical anomalies that mimic other chromatin-remodeling disorders.
